subject: Post-call SLO matrix & reliability next steps — Arcadia Bank
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julia Park <julia@arcadia-bank.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: reliability goals / fallback strategy notes (Arcadia)

Hi Julia — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and agreed next steps so we’re all aligned.

High-level pain points you shared:
- Recent production incidents (see attached summary) where token generation latency spiked and opened up timeouts for downstream pipelines.
- Concern about single-region outages impacting transaction-facing experiences (peak-hours SLA exposure).
- Need for strict audit logs and 12–18 month evidence retention for regulatory reviews.

Current stack you described:
- Primary inference currently served from a managed provider in us-east-1.
- Stateless front-end with synchronous calls to model endpoint (no client-side caching).
- Existing canary routing, but no automated model-fallback or prefix caching in front of the model.

Success criteria you’re evaluating (as I captured):
- P95 request latency < 300ms for token streaming under normal load; 99.9% availability for transaction-critical routes.
- Graceful degradation: meaningful fallback responses (short-form summary) within 50–100ms when primary endpoint is degraded.
- Transparent auditability: per-request trace + 12-month retention of logs/audit trail.

Suggested reliability / graceful-deg approach (next steps we offered):
1) SLO matrix (attached) tailored to your transaction vs. batch flows.
2) Multi-tier fallback plan: lightweight quantized model variant in a secondary region (active-passive) + cached summary responses for very high load.
3) Rollout plan: canary + automated fallback policy; runbook for incident handoff.

Immediate action items / owners:
- Grace: send SLO matrix (attached) and initial proposal (SLO_proposal_v1.pdf) — DONE (attached).
- Arcadia (Julia): confirm whether 12 or 18 months retention is required and share the compliance contact.
- Mateo/Dev: schedule technical deep-dive to validate fallback model feasibility and region failover (Link to calendar below).

Attachments: SLO_matrix_arcadia_v1.xlsx, SLO_proposal_v1.pdf, prod-incident-summary.pdf (you shared during the call).

Proposed timeline:
- Technical deep-dive: within 5 working days
- First SLO & fallback proposal: 1 week after deep-dive

If anything above is off, correct me and I’ll update the matrix. Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0143

--
Redwood Inference — production-first inference for developers

From: Julia Park <julia@arcadia-bank.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: reliability goals / fallback strategy notes (Arcadia)

Hi Grace — thanks for the tidy recap and the SLO doc. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Retention: we need 12 months minimum for audit logs; security may ask for 18 in rare audits but 12 is the baseline.
- Incidents: I attached the internal incident timeline (prod-incident-summary.pdf) you referenced — it shows three notable events in the last 9 months.
- Multi-region: we prefer active-active for user-facing latency, but we'll accept active-passive if active-active has material complexity. Please call out the tradeoffs.

Next for us: please provide an initial pricing delta for the multi-region fallback and the dedicated reserved capacity option (if that materially reduces the cost of guaranteed SLOs). Also include any constraints around encryption-at-rest for cached prefixes.

I’ve copied our security contact incase they want to add anything: security@arcadia-bank.com

Thanks,
Julia Park
Director, Digital Channels | Arcadia Bank
julia@arcadia-bank.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Post-call: reliability goals / fallback strategy notes (Arcadia)

Folks — forwarding Julia’s reply and attached incident summary. Key asks we need to answer:

- Confirm 12 vs 18 month retention (Julia indicated 12 minimum).
- Pricing delta for multi-region (active-active) vs active-passive + impact on cost per 1M tokens.
- Options for encryption-at-rest for prefix caches and audit log retention (KMS/HSM details).
- A concrete fallback model suggestion (size/quantization) that can meet 50–100ms response for short-form fallback.

My quick thoughts:
- Fallback model: a quantized gpt-like 7B variant (redwood-7b-quant) with KV cache priming and a minimal prompt scaffold should be able to return concise fallbacks within target latency in us-west.
- Active-active will require cross-region KV sync or eventual-consistent cached prefixes; complexity increases but user latency improves for global customers.

Can you put together a short risk/feasibility note and one-slide cost delta for the two multi-region options? We should include suggested SLO values (p95, p99 latency and availability) in the slide.

Thanks — cc’ing Julia for visibility.

Counting off items and owners — will put together the deliverables by Friday: 

1) Short feasibility + risk note (Dev, lead): include fallback model benchmarks (latency/throughput) for redwood-7b-quant and a smaller 2B quant variant.
2) Cost delta slide (Mateo): active-active vs active-passive + dedicated reserved capacity option. I’ll include expected cost per 1M tokens and incremental infra premium for cross-region replication.
3) Security brief (Dev): KMS/HSM options for encrypted prefix caches and audit retention mechanisms.
4) Schedule: technical deep-dive — I propose Thu 22 Oct 2026, 10:00–11:00 PT. Link: https://calendar.redwood.ai/event/arcadia-technical-deep-dive

Deliverables will reference the attached SLO matrix (Grace) and the incident timeline. I’ll also add recommended SLO thresholds: p95 latency target 250–300ms, p99 < 600ms for transaction-critical, availability target 99.9%.

Will share a one-slide summary + backup notes by EOD Fri.
